Title: Reclassify cable theft through targeted legal and enforcement reforms
Article:
LETTERS:
The NST special report on increasingly sophisticated and dangerous copper and cable theft is deeply concerning, not only from an operational standpoint but, more importantly, from a public safety perspective.
Any interference with rail signalling, power supply, or control systems introduces risks that extend far beyond inconvenience — they place passengers, frontline workers, and the wider public in harm's way.
It is, therefore, appropriate to raise public awareness which is not a sign of weakness
Transparency helps Malaysians understand that every service disruption, repair, and delay ultimately draws on public funds and affects national productivity.
Cable theft in the rail sector should no longer be viewed as a simple property crime.
The removal of copper and signalling components — often requiring technical knowledge — constitutes tampering with safety‑critical systems.
In many jurisdictions, such acts are treated as offences against public safety and national infrastructure, with penalties reflecting the gravity of the risk created.
Focusing enforcement efforts solely on the individuals caught cutting or stealing cables, many of whom are repeat offenders, risks missing the broader problem.
Experience across multiple sectors — including power, rail, and telecommunications — shows that arresting foot soldiers alone rarely delivers lasting deterrence.
Without addressing the wider mechanics that allow stolen materials to be absorbed quickly into legitimate-looking channels, incidents tend to recur.
This is why Malaysia should consider targeted amendments to existing laws to strengthen deterrence and improve outcomes.
Among the measures worth examining are:
*  Reclassifying cable theft involving rail, power, or communications systems as a public safety offence, with penalties reflecting the potential risk to life.
*  Enhancing powers to act against those who knowingly deal in or facilitate the disposal of stolen infrastructure materials, rather than limiting enforcement to the act of theft alone.
*  Introducing stronger licensing, audit, and compliance requirements for sectors that handle high-risk recyclable materials linked to critical infrastructure.
Such measures would align enforcement with the reality that this is a systemic crime affecting national development, not an isolated nuisance.
Malaysia should also remain open to proven technologies and practices used internationally to protect infrastructure assets.
In several countries, asset-identification and traceability solutions have helped authorities link recovered materials back to their rightful owners, even after attempts have been made to destroy identifying features.
Industry and regulators should be encouraged to study these approaches carefully and adapt what is appropriate for local conditions, rather than assuming that traditional methods alone will suffice against increasingly sophisticated criminal activity.
Transport Minister has indicated that discussions have been held with enforcement agencies and that efforts will be stepped up.
This commitment is important and should translate into visible, sustained action across agencies. Cable theft affects multiple sectors simultaneously, and a fragmented response only benefits those who exploit gaps between jurisdictions.
At the same time, it is crucial that operators like Prasarana are supported, not criticised, for taking proactive steps to protect passengers and assets.
Ensuring safe and reliable public transport is a shared responsibility involving operators, regulators, enforcement agencies, industry, and the public.
Malaysia's progress depends on the integrity and resilience of its critical infrastructure. Addressing cable theft decisively is not merely about preventing losses — it is about protecting lives, safeguarding public confidence, and upholding good governance.
The sooner we treat it as such, the better served the nation will be.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Kuala Lumpur

Title: KFC picks Coca-Cola as US soda supplier, ditches longtime partner PepsiCo
Article:
LOUISVILLE, (United States): Fast-food chain KFC on Thursday signed Coca-Cola as its beverage partner for US stores, bringing to a close a relationship with PepsiCo that dates back about four decades.
The loss of the beverage partnership with KFC, which has 3,718 US locations, could be a setback for PepsiCo as it works to improve soda sales in the country, while its snacks business grapples with high prices and a shift to healthier options.
Higher costs have also added to concerns for PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta, who said earlier this month that growth and margin recovery was taking longer than planned.
The partnership began when PepsiCo acquired KFC in a bid to expand into food and snacks. While PepsiCo later spun off KFC in 1997, it continued to be a beverage partner for its parent Yum Brands.
"It is just a bad look for PepsiCo... when you lose a big-name brand partner like that. This could be the optical straw that breaks the camel's back," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets.
"It is very rare that you have two giants in the same industry take such a different turn," he said. Freedom Capital Markets holds shares in Coca-Cola.
PepsiCo is also under scrutiny from activist investor Elliott Investment Management, which disclosed a stake in the company last year, and has asked it to sell underperforming assets and improve its performance in North America.
Yum Brands and PepsiCo just renewed agreements across Taco Bell and KFC International stores, a spokesperson for PepsiCo told Reuters. Taco Bell is a 10-year agreement, they said.
PepsiCo has beverage partner agreements at sandwich chains Subway and Jersey Mike's Subs.
It also runs the soda fountain at Pizza Hut, which left the Yum Brands umbrella only this year and switched to PepsiCo from Coca-Cola in 2011.
In 2012, PepsiCo lost Dunkin to Coca-Cola after a five-year run at the donut chain.
Coca-Cola products will be available at KFC US restaurants by spring 2027, the company said. Financial details of the partnership were not disclosed.
Coca-Cola is a long-standing beverage partner at burger chains McDonald's and Wendy's.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the news on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Title: Police record 199 criminal cases involving Rohingya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police recorded 199 criminal cases involving Rohingya refugees in the country between 2022 and August 2026.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Selangor recorded the highest number of cases at 58, followed by Kedah with 26 and Kuala Lumpur with 22.
"2022 recorded the highest number of cases at 52, followed by 43 in 2023, 37 in 2024, 29 in 2025 and 38 up to August 2026," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament portal today.
He was responding to Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah), who asked for the number of criminal offences involving Rohingya refugees by state, as well as the government's measures to strengthen control, registration and monitoring of the community to ensure public safety and order.
Saifuddin said National Security Council (NSC) Directive No. 23, on the Policy and Mechanism for the Management of Refugees and Asylum Seekers, was established to manage all groups of refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia comprehensively, rather than focusing solely on the Rohingya community.
He said the directive outlined guidelines and the functions and roles of various ministries and enforcement agencies to safeguard national security.
"Under the framework of NSC Directive No. 23, the government is strengthening control and monitoring of all refugee communities, including the Rohingya, through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme," he said.
He added that the DPP programme served as the government's main instrument to take over and strengthen the centralised management of refugee data, reducing its full dependence on the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
"Migrants whose status has been verified will be issued a special pass in the form of a card known as the DPP card.
"The card serves as an official identity document for this group and is the only document recognised by the government that allows its holders to reside temporarily in Peninsular Malaysia until a final arrangement is made for them," he said.

Title: Oil prices edge down as investors weigh possible US sanctions on 'shadow fleet'
Article:
BEIJING: Oil prices edged down on Friday morning as investors weighed risks in the Middle East and possible US moves to ease restrictions on the world's "shadow fleet" of tankers.
Brent crude futures fell 41 US cents, or 0.39 per cent, to US$105.51 a barrel by 0012 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 54 US cents, or 0.55 per cent, to US$97.43.
WTI settled more than three per cent higher on Thursday after a large drawdown in US crude stocks supported prices, while Brent crude was little changed.
The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel to the market, along with any remaining oil from a record release of emergency reserves pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices.
Oil prices rose overnight during the previous trading session, suggesting that "investors were dissatisfied with these measures", Haitong Futures said in a note on Friday.
"What would really cool the oil market is an easing of tensions in the Middle East."
The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move that drew strong criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans in the US Senate.
Meanwhile, escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, along with renewed attacks on ships in the region, supported prices.
Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
The Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure amid the escalating conflict.

Title: Trump scraps plan to livestream execution after fierce backlash
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday canceled plans to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base mass shooter, reversing a widely condemned move by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The plan to make Nidal Hasan's execution public was opposed at home and abroad, with US Democratic and Republican politicians, the Catholic Church and the United Nations all expressing outrage.
The cancellation is a blow to Hegseth, who is already under fire over the stalemated Iran war and its fallout, which are weighing on Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.
Hasan "will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.
The US president indicated he did not personally oppose the streaming plan, saying it "might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan."
But "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die," Trump said, adding that the execution could still be viewed in person by immediate family of the victims if they wanted to do so.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said Hegseth and Trump had spoken before the announcement.
"The secretary supports the president's decision, and they are completely aligned," Parnell said in a statement.
Hasan's execution – scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 – is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.
Last week, Hegseth said that "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public," later confirming that the plan was to livestream the execution.
"People need to understand that...there's serious consequences for these types of things," he said.
Backlash to the plan quickly grew following Hegseth's announcement.
MOST AMERICANS OPPOSED
The United Nations said streaming the execution would amount to "torture," while the president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said it was a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death," and both Australia and Britain's prime ministers described it as "abhorrent."
A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll released Thursday found that eight in 10 Americans opposed livestreaming the execution.
Lawmakers from both main US parties have said they were against it, and dozens of retired US military officers expressed opposition to the planned broadcast in an open letter.
It "will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," and "will ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr," said the officers, including more than 40 generals and admirals.
Some US Democratic lawmakers on Thursday hailed the decision to cancel the livestream while slamming Hegseth.
Representative Chrissy Houlahan said it was "as clear an illustration as any that Hegseth is dangerously unqualified," while Senator Jack Reed said Trump was "right to backtrack" but that Hegseth "deserves to be admonished for his lack of judgment."
Republican Senator John Curtis also weighed in, saying the cancelation "is the right move, both for the loved ones of the victims and for the country."
The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.
The Death Penalty Information Center says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.
Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralysed from the waist down.
Hasan chose to conduct his own defence during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges.
He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.
The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military's occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

Title: MSCI set to remove Indonesia from global indexes
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, which intends to remove it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, in a major setback likely to trigger capital outflows.
Indonesian equities are already the world's worst performers this year, struggling since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour.
On Friday, it said reforms to address those problems had not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier status would not reflect the severity of the issues.
Instead, it put Indonesia on a path to "standalone" status, which would exclude Indonesian stocks from global indexes tracked by billions of dollars in passive investment, forcing funds that follow or are benchmarked against the indexes to sell.
"Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said in a statement posted on its website. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said.
"Feedback from market participants suggests that a reclassification to frontier markets would not properly recognise the depth of the market problems."
The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday it had taken concrete steps to enhance transparency and integrity in the country's capital market.
The exchange respected MSCI's independence in conducting assessments and would seek further clarification on the basis for the announcement, its chief executive officer Jeffrey Hendrik said in a statement.
Indonesia's Financial Services Authority and Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara, who chairs the country's financial stability board, did not immediately reply to separate requests for comment on the MSCI announcement.
MSCI said it would consult market participants on a downgrade to "standalone" status until April 2027 and then proceed with the reclassification unless it found clear evidence of improvement in market governance and functioning.
Standalone markets are not included in MSCI's emerging or frontier index products, which are tracked by passive funds and serve as performance benchmarks for other fund managers.
MSCI said reclassification to standalone status could occur in cases of severe deterioration in market accessibility, size or liquidity, with Argentina being the most recent example.
Indonesia has faced a series of setbacks this year, with Moody's and Fitch cutting their sovereign rating outlooks to negative, citing reduced policymaking credibility.
The benchmark Jakarta stock index has fallen more than 30 per cent this year, making it the world's worst-performing equity market, with net selling by foreign investors amounting to US$4.7 billion worth of shares.

Title: Customs officer murder: 'The way she died is heartbreaking,' says grieving brother
Article:
NILAI: The death of a 35-year-old female civil servant, allegedly at the hands of her own husband, has left her family heartbroken, particularly over the circumstances surrounding her death.
Her brother, Amran Ibrahim, 59, said the family was struggling to come to terms with the incident, which happened about 7pm yesterday at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA here.
"We accepted it as fate if it was her time to go. However, the way she died is heartbreaking, especially since the person responsible was her own husband," he said when met at the scene early this morning.
Amran said he received a call from his younger brother about 7.30pm informing him that their youngest sister, Norhazwani Ibrahim, had allegedly been killed by her husband.
"At the time, I was at home in Pinggiran Batu Caves, Selangor, when I received a call from my younger brother. He told me that my brother-in-law (the suspect) had contacted him and said he had killed his own wife.
"I had mixed feelings. I was shocked, could not believe it and was also angry. I immediately contacted the police station because the suspect had also said he wanted to turn himself in," he said.
Amran said he later received confirmation of the incident from the police before rushing to the couple's home with other relatives.
He said Norhazwani, known as Wani or Mok Su among family members, had been closer to their eighth sibling than to the rest of the family.
"There are nine of us, and I am the eldest. The last time I saw her was about seven months ago, but we kept in touch through WhatsApp.
"Only three of us live in the Klang Valley, while the others, including our eighth sibling, live in Kelantan.
"Yesterday (Wednesday), he visited Wani's house and stayed overnight because he had some matters to attend to here.
"He even reminded her to take good care of her marriage. We never expected something so shocking to happen that night," he said.
Amran said the suspect was believed to have been released from prison a few days earlier after serving time for a drug-related offence.
The couple were also believed to be in the process of getting a divorce.
Describing his sister as cheerful and well-liked by family members and colleagues, Amran said her employer had offered to help arrange for her remains to be taken to Pengkalan Kubor, Tumpat, Kelantan, for burial.
"For now, we need to settle the post-mortem arrangements at Hospital Tuanku Ja'afar in Seremban first. It is expected to be conducted on Saturday.
"Other family members may wait in our hometown, while I will handle the arrangements here with relatives who live nearby," he said.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad was
reported
to have confirmed that the woman, a Customs Department officer, was found murdered at the government quarters.
He said the murder was believed to have been committed by her husband, who surrendered himself at a police station after the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.

Title: Shooter killed at Oregon elementary school; CNN, CBS report four dead in violence
Article:
OREGON: A person with a gun opened fire on Thursday at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, wounding multiple victims, including children, before the assailant was killed, possibly by an armed onlooker, according to police.
CNN and CBS News, citing law enforcement sources, reported that one adult and three children were killed in the violence, but it was not immediately clear whether the shooter was included in that death toll.
Both news outlets reported later that the shooter was 16 years of age, with CNN describing the teen as a boy.
Police in Bend, a city of about 100,000 residents in rural central Oregon, 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, said the first call they received from the 1 p.m. (2000 GMT) incident "indicated that an unknown man had shot into a car" at Silver Rail Elementary School.
Moments later, emergency dispatchers received multiple calls "reporting that a person had entered the school and begun shooting," police said in a statement.
Officers arriving seconds later found that the suspect had been shot dead, possibly by a bystander, according to police.
Sheila Miller, a spokesperson for the Bend Police Department, told reporters investigators had yet to confirm who shot the suspect.
Miller said that at least two victims were transported to a hospital but she was unaware of their condition. The subsequent police statement, posted online, said authorities "have confirmed there were multiple victims," with at least two taken to hospital, adding, "Children are among the victims."
Silver Rail Elementary School serves kindergarten through fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, in Bend, situated in the Oregon high desert adjacent to the Deschutes National Forest. It has about 450 students and 40 staff members, Miller said.
US Representative Maxine Dexter, a physician who represents a portion of Portland east of the Willamette River, called the shooting a "devastating day for Oregon."
"Schools should be places of learning, friendship and joy. It is incumbent on me, and every lawmaker, to do everything we can to ensure our kids are safe," she said in a statement.
"As we learn more about the tragic event at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend today, we must come together and support each other, neighbor to neighbor, Oregonian to Oregonian. No community should have to live through this day," Governor Tina Kotek said separately on X.
FBI chief Kash Patel said on X that federal agents were on the scene "assisting our local partners in the investigation" and that his agency would "make every resource they need available."

Title: Listening to understand, not simply to answer
Article:
IN the workplace, communication is often regarded as the key to effective collaboration. We are encouraged to express our thoughts clearly, share ideas confidently and contribute meaningfully to discussions.
Yet, amid all this emphasis on speaking, we sometimes overlook one of the most important aspects of communication: listening.
More importantly, we forget that there is a fundamental difference between listening to understand and listening simply to answer.
Many of us listen with the intention of responding. While someone is speaking, we are already formulating our reply, preparing a counterargument or thinking about how to demonstrate our knowledge.
We may hear every word, but hearing is not the same as understanding. When our minds are occupied with what we want to say next, we risk missing what the other person is actually trying to communicate.
Listening to understand requires a different mindset. It demands that we temporarily set aside our assumptions, opinions and a desire to respond.
Instead, we give the speaker our attention and make a genuine effort to understand their perspective.
This does not mean we must agree with everything we hear. It simply means we are willing to understand before we judge, evaluate or respond.
This distinction matters enormously in the workplace, where people with different experiences, personalities, responsibilities and expectations must work together.
Misunderstandings can arise when instructions are incomplete, concerns are dismissed or differing viewpoints are interpreted as challenges to authority.
Sometimes, what appears to be resistance is actually uncertainty. What sounds like criticism may be a genuine attempt to improve a situation.
Without listening carefully, we may respond to what we assume was meant rather than what was actually said.
The consequences can extend beyond a single conversation. When people repeatedly feel unheard, they become less willing to speak openly.
They may stop raising concerns, offering suggestions or questioning decisions that deserve closer examination.
Silence can then be mistaken for agreement, when it may simply reflect frustration, resignation or a belief that speaking up will make little difference.
Conversely, when people feel genuinely heard, trust begins to develop. They are more likely to share information, acknowledge mistakes and discuss difficulties honestly.
They understand that their contributions matter, even when their opinions differ from those of their colleagues or supervisors.
This creates an environment in which disagreements can be addressed constructively rather than allowed to grow into resentment.
Good listening is particularly important for those in leadership positions. Authority may compel people to follow instructions, but it does not automatically earn their trust or respect.
Leaders who listen demonstrate that they value the knowledge and experiences of others. They also give themselves access to perspectives that might otherwise remain hidden.
No individual, regardless of seniority or experience, possesses all the answers.
There is also a practical benefit to listening before responding. Taking the time to understand a problem properly can prevent unnecessary mistakes, wasted effort and avoidable conflict.
Asking a few thoughtful questions at the beginning of a conversation may save hours of correcting an outcome based on an incorrect assumption.
In this sense, listening is not merely a social courtesy. It is an essential part of sound judgement and effective decision-making.
Of course, listening well is not always easy. We may feel defensive when challenged, impatient when conversations move slowly or distracted by the pressures of our daily responsibilities.
Personal biases can also influence how we interpret what others say. We tend to give greater weight to opinions that reinforce our existing beliefs and may dismiss those that make us uncomfortable.
Recognising these tendencies is an important first step towards becoming better listeners.
The practice itself need not be complicated. Give the speaker your full attention. Resist the temptation to interrupt. Ask questions when something is unclear.
Where appropriate, summarise what you have heard to check that you have understood correctly. Most importantly, allow the other person to finish expressing their thoughts before preparing your response.
These simple habits communicate respect and reduce the likelihood of misunderstanding.
There will, naturally, be times when we must disagree, correct an error or make a difficult decision.
Listening to understand does not require endless discussion or the abandonment of conviction. Rather, it ensures that our responses are informed by a fair understanding of the circumstances.
We can disagree without being dismissive, challenge an idea without belittling its author and make decisions without making others feel insignificant.
Ultimately, the quality of workplace communication depends not only on how effectively we express ourselves but also on how sincerely we receive what others have to say.
We cannot expect people to understand our intentions if we are unwilling to understand theirs.
Perhaps the simplest test of good listening is this: after a conversation, can the other person feel confident that we understood what they were trying to communicate, even if we did not agree with them?
If the answer is yes, we have achieved something far more valuable than winning an argument or delivering a clever response.
The next time someone speaks to us at work, we should resist the urge to prepare an answer before they have finished.
Instead, we should listen with curiosity, patience and an open mind. After all, the purpose of communication is not simply to ensure that our voices are heard. It is to ensure that understanding is achieved.

Title: Q3 2027 GDP to moderate, as consumer remains cautious
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic growth is expected to moderate in the third quarter of 2026 as resilient exports and investment help offset cautious consumer spending amid rising costs, economists said.
The economy expanded six per cent year-on-year in the second quarter, following 5.4 per cent growth in the first quarter, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent.
Exports rose 45.5 per cent year-on-year to RM191.1 billion in August, driven by a 66.5 per cent increase in electrical and electronics products amid strong demand for semiconductors and artificial intelligence-related equipment.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expects gross domestic product (GDP) to expand 5.2 per cent in the July-September quarter.
Meanwhile, Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid forecasts growth of 5.0 per cent.
The projections point to slower growth from the six per cent recorded in the second quarter and 5.4 per cent in the first quarter, following stronger economic activity in the first half of the year.
Afzanizam said the economic landscape remained resilient during the quarter, particularly in terms of external demand, although higher living costs could make consumers and businesses more cautious in their spending.
He said the producer price index (PPI), which rose 10.7 per cent in August, could signal that businesses would gradually pass on higher input costs to consumers.
"Domestic demand is likely to remain resilient, although at the same time, remain fairly cautious," he said.
Afzanizam expects Malaysia's GDP growth to reach around 5.2 per cent for the full year 2026.
Aimi said the projected third-quarter growth of five per cent would remain at the upper end of the government's official full-year growth forecast of four to 4.5 per cent.
He identified strong demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products, particularly those linked to artificial intelligence (AI), alongside domestic investment and private consumption as the main drivers supporting growth.
Aimi said investment in machinery and equipment, information and communications technology, and data centres would provide additional support to economic activity.
Private consumption, meanwhile, would continue to be supported by a stable labour market, wage growth and government cash assistance, although higher costs could temper spending.
He said the outlook remained exposed to external risks, including potential US tariffs on semiconductors and escalating tensions in the Middle East.
EXPORT GROWTH OUTPACES IMPORTS
Malaysia's trade performance continued to provide support to economic growth, with exports expanding faster than imports in the first eight months of 2026.
Exports increased 31.2 per cent year-on-year to RM1.356 trillion between January and August, while imports rose 22.4 per cent to RM1.158 trillion.
This resulted in a trade surplus of RM198.7 billion, up 127.6 per cent from a year earlier, according to the figures provided by Aimi.
However, he cautioned that strong export growth did not necessarily translate into an equivalent increase in domestic value-add, as manufacturers also relied on imported intermediate goods and components.
August imports of intermediate goods rose 50.5 per cent to RM90.7 billion, while capital goods imports increased 37.4 per cent to RM21.6 billion. Imports of consumption goods fell 1.6 per cent to RM9.3 billion.
The composition suggested that import demand was being driven largely by production and investment requirements rather than household consumption, Aimi said.
TRADE IMBALANCES WITH US AND CHINA
Aimi also highlighted Malaysia's contrasting trade positions with the United States and China, describing them as interconnected with the restructuring of global supply chains.
Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM101.5 billion with the US in 2025, while its trade deficit with China reached RM163.4 billion.
The deficit with China had widened to RM159.8 billion in the first eight months of 2026, based on the figures provided.
He said Malaysia had benefited from the China-plus-one strategy, as companies diversified manufacturing and sourcing away from China amid higher US tariffs.
However, Malaysian manufacturers continued to depend on intermediate components from China and other regional suppliers to produce goods for export, particularly in the E&E sector.
This meant that stronger exports to the US could coincide with higher imports from China, reflecting Malaysia's role in regional production networks.
Aimi said the challenge was to increase domestic value-added by encouraging local companies, particularly small and medium enterprises, to produce more raw materials and semi-finished products currently imported for manufacturing.
He added that greater domestic production capabilities and more diversified export markets and import sources would help Malaysia capture a larger share of the value generated by international trade.
"The policy challenge for 2027 is not to close the China deficit with protectionism, but to increase domestic value-added," he said.

Title: Ringgit opens flat against US dollar as markets assess US interest rate outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened flat against the US dollar on Friday as expectations of restrictive US monetary policy offset support from a weaker greenback.
At 8am, the ringgit was almost unchanged at 4.0800/0845 against the US dollar, compared with Thursday's close of 4.0800/0835.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.53 per cent to 102.005 points, alongside a decline in Brent crude oil prices to around US$105 per barrel.
However, persistent US inflationary pressures and expectations that the US Federal Reserve (Fed) would maintain its restrictive monetary policy could temper the ringgit's gains.
Mohd Afzanizam also said the International Energy Agency's (IEA) pledge to withdraw 100 million barrels of oil from its reserves has calmed the oil market, albeit momentarily, as supply disruptions remained unresolved.
At the same time, he said valuation concerns in artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks triggered a flight-to-safety move, which drove down US Treasury yields.
"Still, the latest print on the US Producer Price Index (PPI) reading for September suggested that the inflation rate remains elevated, with the index rising 6.3 per cent, exceeding the consensus forecast of 5.3 per cent. This could mean the Fed is likely to maintain its restrictive posture at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting at the end of this month." Mohd Afzanizam told Bernama.
On the domestic front, the market would be focusing on the release of Malaysia's advance estimate of third quarter (3Q) 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) today.
"We foresee that the provisional figure could reach around 5.2 per cent, although slower than the 6.0 per cent growth recorded in 2Q 2026, we still think the growth remains decent as it continues to grow above its trend level. Hence, the anticipation of normalisation of the overnight policy rate (OPR) would provide support to the ringgit," he said.
Mohd Afzanizam expects the US dollar-ringgit pair to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.09 today.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly firmer against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5797/5827 from 2.5869/5892 at Thursday's close, advanced against the euro to  4.5741/5791 from 4.5761/5801, but fell against the British pound to 4.4138/4197 from 4.4101/4147 yesterday.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit traded mixed.
It was almost flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 227.4/227.8 from 227.4/227.7 at Thursday's close, and remained unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.47/6.48.

Title: Singapore exports rise 68.4pct in September
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports rose 68.4 per cent year-on-year in September, marking the sixth consecutive month of growth above 20 per cent, according to government data.
The increase was driven mainly by non-electronic exports, particularly ships and boats, while electronic exports also recorded strong growth.
The expansion exceeded the median forecast of 32.2 per cent growth in a Reuters poll.
Electronics exports surged 107.6 per cent year-on-year in September, while non-electronic exports rose 54.2 per cent, Enterprise Singapore said in a statement.
Exports to nine of Singapore's top 10 markets increased, with shipments to Hong Kong surging 112.1 per cent.
In August, Enterprise Singapore raised its forecast for non-oil domestic export growth this year to between 14 and 16 per cent, from its earlier projection of three to five per cent.

Title: Pas to prioritise Umno, BN in GE16 negotiations
Article:
ARAU: Pas will prioritise Umno and Barisan Nasional over other political parties in any negotiations for the next general election (GE16).
Pas spiritual leader Datuk Hashim Jasin said the decision was made at a recent Syura Council meeting he chaired, which gave the central leadership a mandate to negotiate with any party, with Umno given priority.
He said the council believed bringing Pas and Umno together was not easy and that the opportunity should be fully utilised.
"Whoever Pas chooses to cooperate with, Umno must not be left behind.
"The unity between Pas and Umno must be preserved, and they must be prioritised in negotiations," he said when met yesterday.
Hashim added that unity between the two Malay-Muslim parties must be built on the interests of the Malays and Islam rather than political considerations.
He warned that alliances built solely for political survival would fail.
"The previous Muafakat Nasional charter served as the foundation, and now is the time to revive unity between both parties.
"Within Umno, we are seeing growing awareness of the importance of this unification," he said.
Hashim said Pas felt more comfortable cooperating with Umno than with other parties, adding that the people wanted unity between the two Malay-Muslim parties.
On the Melaka state election, he said Pas was prepared to contest under its own logo if Perikatan Nasional was unable to field candidates under the coalition banner.
"Pas will use its own logo, while Umno or BN can use theirs, but we will still work together in the state election.
There is no issue regarding the logo.
"As for seat allocations, it is up to the Pas central leadership to decide whether to give up our seats or not. What matters most is that negotiations with Umno remain the priority," he said.

Title: Haze: Johor worst hit as Pasir Gudang records very unhealthy API of 203

In Negri Sembilan, Nilai recorded a reading of 189, followed by Seremban (181) and Port Dickson (171).
In Melaka, Bandaraya Melaka recorded a reading of 178, followed by Bukit Rambai (177) and Alor Gajah (170).
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded a reading of 173, followed by Tanjung Malim (164), Pegoh Ipoh (156) and Tasek Ipoh (153).

Title: Venezuela's Maduro, wife plead not guilty to new US torture charges
Article:
NEW YORK: Ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores pleaded not guilty Thursday to new torture charges brought against the pair held in US custody since their extraordinary capture in January.
They appeared at a New York court after prosecutors alleged they conspired to commit acts including waterboardings, rapes and beatings against victims, including American citizens, in Venezuelan detention.
Maduro, who has previously called himself a "prisoner of war," slammed the latest charges as "false allegations."
The couple already face drug trafficking and firearms charges in the United States after they were snatched from their Caracas compound in a US military raid.
According to an indictment, the pair used torture to "intimidate, harass, and neutralize their opponents, including through kidnappings."
During his 2013-2026 presidency, rights groups widely accused Maduro of using political repression to cling to power.
Maduro and Flores are slated for a trial in New York next June and are being held in a Brooklyn jail.
They have appealed to have the charges against them dismissed, claiming they have immunity as president and first lady of a sovereign country.
Since Maduro's capture, his vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, has governed Venezuela as interim leader under intense pressure from US President Donald Trump's administration.

Title: Experts urge clear rules for seizing assets of drunk drivers [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Amendments to current laws to allow the seizure of assets of alcohol- or drug-impaired drivers who fail to compensate their victims must have clear procedures for identifying, valuing and recovering such assets.
Universiti Putra Malaysia Road Safety Research Centre head Associate Professor Dr Law Teik Hua such procedures must also protect third parties and allow offenders to challenge seizures they considered excessive.
He said judicial discretion would also be necessary to assess offenders' actual financial circumstances and distinguish genuine hardship from attempts to evade payment.
He said the government should establish a formal compensation mechanism within criminal proceedings, with courts determining the amount payable based on the severity of the crash, damage incurred and the circumstances of each case.
Law proposed requiring offenders to declare their assets, setting realistic payment schedules and deadlines, and introducing enforcement measures to ensure compliance.
Law was responding to Transport Minister Anthony Loke's statement in the Dewan Rakyat earlier that the government was formulating a mechanism to seize assets and impose additional jail terms on drunk or drug-impaired drivers who failed to pay compensation to crash victims or the families of those killed.
Loke said the measures were intended to ensure compensation orders under amendments to the Road Transport Act provided meaningful recourse, particularly when offenders claimed they could not afford to pay.
He said the Transport Ministry planned to table the amendments in Parliament early next year.
Law said both the seizure of assets and the additional jail terms must be applied together if the amendments were to work.
He said this was the only way to strengthen enforcement and deter offences, while at the same time ensuring that victims, or their families, were compensated.
He said asset recovery could provide financial restitution to road crash victims and the families of those killed, while additional imprisonment would punish offenders who failed to comply with court orders.
"Relying solely on longer jail terms might not ensure victims receive the compensation to which they are entitled.
"The policy effectiveness of proposed amendments hinges critically on whether asset recovery will supplement punitive sanctions."
Law said asset seizures could be effective against offenders with sufficient financial resources and identifiable assets, helping address claims that they could not afford to pay.
"However, determining whether an offender is genuinely unable to pay could prove challenging, particularly when assets are transferred to third parties, ownership is concealed or properties are jointly owned."
He  said the government should also consider establishing a victim compensation fund to provide provisional payments to affected victims and bereaved families while authorities pursue the recovery of offenders' assets.
"Insurance companies should also coordinate their payments with the compensation process to avoid duplication and minimise delays."

Title: Singapore weighs action against companies link to transboundary haze, says PM Wong
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore is looking into companies that may be responsible for forest fires in Indonesia, which have worsened haze conditions in the region, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said.
He said the government would take action under the Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act where warranted, while exploring the possibility of joint action with other countries.
"The haze stems from forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, made worse by the extended dry period.
"We have offered our assistance to Indonesia, and will continue working closely with them and our ASEAN partners to address the issue," he said in his Facebook post on Thursday night.
Wong noted that the government will do everything it can to protect Singaporeans, while working with neighbour countries to address the underlying causes of the haze.
"We cannot control the weather or the winds, nor can we directly control what happens beyond our borders," he said, adding that the government will ensure that support is available to those who need it. – BERNAMA

Title: Cops step up K9 patrols at KLIA
Article:

SEPANG: Police have stepped up K9 unit patrols at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), particularly during peak hours, following several recent security incidents.
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M. Ravi said the patrols, previously conducted periodically, had been increased to bolster security at the airport.
He said deployments were planned around peak periods.
"The deployment is not 24 hours a day because the dogs also need rest. We have to identify peak hours and deploy them at appropriate times," he said.
Ravi said patrols also took into account airport users' sensitivities, with handlers and their dogs deployed outside the terminal, including around entrances.
A check at KLIA Terminal 1 yesterday found K9 units patrolling outside, particularly at the departure and arrival levels.
The K9 units are part of security measures to monitor entrances and other areas frequented by airport users.
Their presence alongside other policemen strengthens security monitoring as authorities step up patrols at strategic locations.

Title: 'Great to be back!' Harry, Meghan in first joint outing since UK return
Article:
NOTTINGHAM, United Kingdom: Britain's Prince Harry and his wife on Thursday carried out their first joint engagement since their surprise move back to the UK in August, with Meghan telling wellwishers: "It's great to be back."
King Charles III's 42-year-old younger son and Meghan, 45 – who left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud – were greeted with cheers as they arrived in the central English city of Nottingham.
The couple then stopped to chat and joke with the crowd as well as pose for selfies, give hugs and accept flowers.
The quasi-royal visit potentially puts the pair at odds with Buckingham Palace over their status while living back in Britain.
The king made it clear in a letter released last month that their position was "akin to private citizens" with charitable interests rather than public figures and that they should not be addressed as his and her royal highness.
Known formally as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, the last time Harry and Meghan appeared together at a public event in Britain was when they attended the late Queen Elizabeth II's funeral in September 2022.
Meghan, dressed in a long burgundy winter coat and wearing her hair in a ponytail, at one point kissed a woman on the cheek after she presented her with a gift.
Harry, in a dark suit and open-necked white shirt, bent down to speak to one youngster and told the crowd it was "very nice" to see everyone.
The couple were in the city to visit three charities that support young people and local communities through music, film, sport and tackling food poverty.
FAMILY RIFT
Following a spectacular falling out with the rest of the royal family, Harry and Meghan have sought to build bridges with Charles – but they remain estranged from Harry's older brother and heir to the throne, Prince William.
King Charles meanwhile visited Wales, where he addressed the Welsh parliament.
Anti-monarchy protesters could be heard chanting "Not my King" and "Down, down, down with the Crown" as Charles and Queen Camilla arrived, according to reports.
Charles, who was known as the Prince of Wales until his accession to the throne, has long had a close association with the country, one of the four territories that make up the United Kingdom.
Harry and Meghan settled in California six years ago, but in a surprise move in August they returned to live in the United Kingdom with their two young children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five.
PRIVATE CITIZENS
The late Queen Elizabeth II made it clear to Harry and Meghan before her death in 2022 that there was no "half-in/half-out" option under which they could pursue commercial ventures while being working royals.
A letter issued last month by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the Royal Household, said it was "well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the sovereign and are no longer working members of the royal family."
"Working royals" are members of the royal family who carry out official duties on behalf of the monarch. They receive administrative and other support from the Royal Household to do so.
There are currently seven senior working royals – King Charles and Queen Camilla; son and heir Prince William and his wife Catherine, Princess of Wales; Charles's sister Princess Anne, brother Edward and the latter's wife Sophie.
Other working royals include several of the late Queen Elizabeth II's cousins.

Title: Cheaper essentials for military personnel, veterans at Pernama
Article:

KUALA LUMPUR: Military personnel and veterans will be able to buy essential goods at discounted prices throughout the year under a Defence Ministry initiative offered through Malaysian Armed Forces Trading Corporation (Pernama) outlets.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the Harga Istimewa, Tentera Sejahtera (HITS) initiative would offer discounts of up to 30 per cent on 308 items at all 80 Pernama outlets nationwide.
He said the initiative was part of broader efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel.
He said the ministry had introduced various initiatives involving housing, healthcare, education, skills development and economic opportunities, with HITS focusing on reducing daily expenses for military families.
"Pernama will play a big role in offering goods at truly affordable prices, even lower than retail prices," he said after launching HITS at Pernama Kem Terendak in Melaka yesterday.

Title: Ambani's Jio seeks US$3.2b in record India IPO
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
MUMBAI: India's Jio Platforms Ltd, the digital arm of conglomerate Reliance Industries Ltd, is aiming to raise more than US$3 billion in what would be the country's biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), after announcing pricing details ahead of next week's launch.
The company, controlled by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, is looking to sell 270 million new shares at 1,065-1,119 rupees each, it said on Wednesday.
A sale at the top end of the range would raise around US$3.2 billion, surpassing the previous national IPO record of US$2.9 billion set by Hyundai Motor India Ltd in 2024.
The IPO opens for subscriptions on Oct 21, with a view to listing a week later.
Reliance Industries, India's most valuable listed company, has been pushing to expand beyond its traditional oil refining and petrochemicals businesses into telecommunications, digital services and green energy, with Jio Platforms at the heart of that strategy.
While Jio has expanded into areas ranging from artificial intelligence to enterprise network services, it is best known for telecommunications subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, India's largest mobile operator by subscribers.
Launched a decade ago, Jio's wireless service disrupted the market with steep discounts that helped it rapidly win customers from rivals Bharti Airtel Ltd and Vodafone Group plc.
The carrier has more than 530 million subscribers and handles roughly 60 per cent of India's mobile data traffic.
The company raised more than US$20 billion in 2020 from global investors and technology giants, including Meta Platforms Inc and Alphabet Inc, funding an ambitious digital ecosystem spanning payments, entertainment streaming and online services. — REUTERS

Title: Mexico gives social networks one month to remove violent content
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
MEXICO CITY: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on Wednesday ordered Meta, TikTok, X, Apple and Microsoft to remove content inciting violence on their social networks following a spate of deadly attacks in schools.
Sheinbaum gave the platforms a month to comply or face sanctions.
In the past two weeks, two people have been killed and several others have been injured in two separate school attacks.
The attacks have caused alarm in a country that lives in terror of brutal drug cartels but is a relative stranger to shootings or stabbings in schools.
On Oct 1, two teenage brothers armed with knives and fireworks killed a female assistant principal and injured three other people at a school in Coahuila state.
Then on Tuesday, a teacher was shot dead at a school in the southern state of Oaxaca.
Sheinbaum linked the violence to "behaviour associated with communication on social media".
She said that if the tech companies did not "adjust their algorithms" to remove "all violent content linked to the accounts of children and adolescents", she would legislate to impose sanctions on them.
The decree issued by Sheinbaum orders social networks to prevent minors accessing "images and videos that lead to or encourage violence in a school setting", including "abuse, suicide, self-harm, cyberbullying and hate speech".
The networks must alert the authorities "if they identify content that endangers life".
In a discussion with TikTok and Instagram users, Sheinbaum denied that the new rules amounted to censorship.
"We're not banning social media," she said. — AFP

Title: Police confirm Customs officer murdered by husband at KLIA quarters

Title: Tuition teacher held over sexual assault, unnatural sex involving five boys
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A tuition teacher has been arrested to assist investigations into sexual assault and unnatural sex involving five male pupils.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the offences took place at the suspect's house, which was also used as a tuition centre.
He said police had received five separate reports involving teenage and child victims, all lodged at the Bukit Jalil police station.
"The first police report was lodged on Oct 6, followed by a second on Oct 10, while three more reports were received on Oct 11," he said in a statement.
Fadil said police had conducted detailed investigations and recorded statements from various parties.
"Further investigations have been carried out, and police have recorded statements from the victims and their family members.
"All parties, including the victims' families, schools and the District Education Office, have fully cooperated with the investigation," he said.
He confirmed that the suspect had been arrested and remanded to facilitate further investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Section 377C of the Penal Code and Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act," he said.

Title: Student raises questions over donations to Najib
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A student representative has questioned public donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, raising concerns over fundraising efforts for a leader convicted in the SRC International case.
Ummi Umairah Bakhit of Universiti Malaya raised the issue during a dialogue with former minister Khairy Jamaluddin, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
She expressed surprise at the public's willingness to contribute to Najib's fundraising campaign, citing the former prime minister's legal cases linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
"The stupidest thing I have watched in my entire life is people donating to our former prime minister, Najib Razak, someone who clearly has a worldwide corruption case, 1MDB, and is clearly linked to corruption," she said.
The Najib Razak Solidarity Fund was set up on Sept 18 following the Federal Territories Pardons Board's announcement that Najib had been granted a conditional pardon.
Under the decision, Najib was allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house detention until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in connection with his conviction in the SRC International case.
On Sept 27, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party had collected RM9.25 million for the fund.
Ummi also referred to the Tabung Haji controversy and sought the panellists' views on corruption and political accountability.
Her questions have since attracted attention on social media platforms, including TikTok and Instagram, where clips of the exchange drew likes and shares.
Reactions were mixed, with some users praising her willingness to raise the issues with political leaders, while others expressed differing views.
She posed the questions during the third edition of iFUTURE, held from Oct 11 to 13, which carried the theme "Redefining Future Leaders Through Value-Based Leadership".
The summit brought together 1,231 student leaders from 20 Malaysian public universities and 30 international universities, including 406 international participants from 53 countries and 310 Johorean university students.
Organised by the Higher Education Ministry through the Department of Higher Education, the summit provided a platform for dialogue between student leaders and figures from government, industry and academia.

Title: Student leader raises corruption concerns with MBs, Khairy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Universiti Malaya student representative today sought the views of two menteris besar and a former health minister on corruption, asking how political leaders should address allegations of wrongdoing and encourage young Malaysians to speak up.
Ummi Umairah Bakhit raised the questions during a Universiti Malaya dialogue attended by Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
She cited reports of alleged corruption involving political figures, including allegations that the son of a political figure had received RM4 million without working.
She asked the panellists to state their positions on corruption and other controversies, including the Tabung Haji controversy and the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
She also sought their advice on how young Malaysians could speak up against corruption and feudalism, think critically and use facts and statistical data to assess issues involving public figures.
In response, Khairy said corruption should be discussed openly, regardless of whether political leaders were involved, and urged the public to take a principled stand against wrongdoing.
"We shouldn't be afraid about talking about corruption. Even if it involves our leaders. We should not be afraid to talk about it. What is wrong is wrong. What you cannot defend, don't defend," he said.
Citing the Malay proverb "Jangan menegakkan benang yang basah" (don't try to stand a wet thread), he said wrongdoing and mismanagement should not be defended and those responsible should be held accountable.
"Never ever compromise when it comes to integrity," he said.
Amirudin said the younger generation's growing focus on corruption was a positive development, noting that the issue had not always played a decisive role in determining electoral outcomes.
He said corruption had been a recurring concern since the 1990s but became a significant factor in the change of government in 2018.
He welcomed young Malaysians' continued attention to the issue, describing it as an encouraging sign.
Onn Hafiz described corruption as a major obstacle to development, saying it could undermine the country's progress.
"I think it is a cancer, and it has a serious negative impact when it comes to progress," he said.
He said everyone should oppose corruption, regardless of whether it involved political leaders, individuals or businesses.
The third edition of iFUTURE, held from Oct 11 to 13, carried the theme "Redefining Future Leaders Through Value-Based Leadership".
The summit brought together 1,231 student leaders from 20 Malaysian public universities and 30 international universities, including 406 international participants from 53 countries and 310 Johorean university students.

Title: Indonesia tests dry ice to disperse haze in South Sumatra
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia has begun testing the use of dry ice to disperse thick haze caused by forest fires in South Sumatra, deploying 1,600kg in an experimental weather modification operation yesterday.
National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre acting head Berton Panjaitan said the operation involved two flights, each carrying 800kg of dry ice, targeting areas around Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II International Airport in Palembang.
"Preliminary reports indicate an improvement in visibility around the seeding area, from approximately 650 metres to 2,800 metres," he said in a statement.
South Sumatra is among Indonesia's six priority provinces for forest and land fire suppression, alongside Riau, Jambi, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan.
Berton said the operation used a Cessna Caravan aircraft, which departed from Raden Inten II Airport in neighbouring Lampung province and dispersed dry ice at an altitude of about 4,500 feet.
He said the technique aimed to disrupt atmospheric conditions that trap thick smoke near the ground, allowing it to rise and disperse to improve visibility.
Unlike conventional weather modification, which uses sodium chloride to stimulate rainfall, the dry ice technique does not depend on the availability of rain clouds, he said.
The trial is scheduled to continue until Oct 18, after which the results will be evaluated and further discussions held with relevant parties on whether to expand the technique to other areas affected by forest and land fires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pilgrims caught up in Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
Article:
PILGRIMS in Saudi Arabia  may not have anticipated being caught up in an air war, but some experienced an attack by Yemen's Houthis first-hand and others have been forced to change their plans.
Footage of the blast that killed 13 people and wounded 300 in a Riyadh airport departure terminal struck  on Saturday showed many passengers attired in the simple white clothes of Muslim pilgrims travelling to Makkah.
Saudi media reported that a Bangladeshi imam leading a group of dozens of pilgrims was killed and others wounded in the attack.
While the Houthis have promised not to attack Makkah and Madinah, the two holiest places in Islam that attract millions of pilgrims each year, they are targeting other Saudi airports in what they call retaliation for Saudi attacks on them.
"I feel deeply worried for my family and myself," said Fadi Anwar, a Jordanian living in Makkah.
"We constantly receive warnings (phone alerts from the authorities) and it causes us great anxiety."
Saudi officials have said the kingdom is safe and that the security of visitors is valued above all else, an offer of reassurance even as Western governments have warned against using most Saudi airports.
Although most international pilgrims fly directly into Madinah  or Jeddah airports, many others travel via Saudi Arabia's other main air hubs, including the many pilgrims who already live in the kingdom.
Al Amin Hassan Mohammed from Sudan, who was visiting Saudi-based family members before a pilgrimage to Makkah, said he had been in Riyadh during Saturday's attack, which sent him and neighbours onto the street.
"We were tired and worried. We went out of the houses and we talked with each other," he said.
Mohammed, who has a married daughter in Saudi Arabia's  city of Dammam, close to Dhahran where the Houthis targeted a Saudi Arabian Oil Company  building on Tuesday, has made the pilgrimage to Makkah before.
The vast courtyard of the enormous main mosque in Makkah was a swirl of pilgrims in their white robes on Tuesday, as they circled the Kaabah, the point towards which all Muslims face to pray.
Makkah draws millions of people each year, both during haj and for umrah, from both inside Saudi Arabia and overseas, and the attacks have made some nervous.
The strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-allied Houthis, resulting from the reignition of Yemen's civil war as a spillover from the United States-Iran conflict, have caused Saudi Arabia to ground many flights.
Schools in Riyadh have been switched to online learning this week and some offices have told staff to work from home.
The disruption has been particularly acute for those trying to travel, a group that includes pilgrims, business figures attending Saudi Arabia's many high-profile conferences, Saudi tourists wishing to go on holiday and foreign residents wanting to fly home.
"We've had some trips postponed. We had friends who were travelling; it was delayed, they didn't travel," said Mohammed.
His friends had been planning to fly via Riyadh but in the end they took a boat back to Sudan from Jeddah, he said.
A senior executive Reuters spoke to on Wednesday was busy arranging transport for foreign employees, sending them by road to Doha in Qatar for onward flights.
A diplomat in Riyadh said several embassies had also used Doha for trips to and from Saudi Arabia over recent days, including for staff temporarily leaving with their families.
The representative of a company organising transport to Doha and Dubai said fares to those destinations had doubled.
Being prepared to pay is no guarantee of travel — in the early phases of the US-Iran war, Iranian fire grounded many flights around the Gulf and that direct conflict may erupt again with US President Donald Trump threatening to resume strikes.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
